title: Conductor Zero-Execution Postmortem v2: 51-milestone SKIP cascade root cause
honest_verdict: complete: pre_test_cascade identified — broken tests/python/inference/test_hw_dab.py imports torch (not installed) + MAX_HEAL_ATTEMPTS=0 disables self-heal → conductor SKIPs every task whenever HEAD~1..HEAD diff pulls the broken file into the smart subset
root_causes_identified: PRIMARY: tests/python/inference/test_hw_dab.py (introduced 2026-05-16 by exp2133, commit 8ade7c530) imports torch as a top-level statement; torch is NOT installed in the .venv. Any conductor pre-test iteration whose `git diff --name-only HEAD~1` returns tests/python/inference/test_hw_dab.py adds that file to the smart subset, pytest collection errors, run_tests() returns (False, ...), every task SKIPs.

AMPLIFIER: scripts/research_conductor.py:4085 sets MAX_HEAL_ATTEMPTS = 0 (intentional, per 2026-05-03 ~11:45Z operator emergency — self-heal burned ~40 min per retiring task). With self-heal disabled, a single pre-test failure cascades into permanent SKIP for every task in the milestone.

PROPAGATION: smart-subset filter at scripts/research_conductor.py:1119 picks up any changed file matching `tests/python/*.py`; the inference subdirectory is included since 'tests/python/inference/' startswith 'tests/python/'. Quarantine filter at line 1124 only skips '/quarantine/' substrings.

RECOVERY MECHANISM (currently active, fragile): the cascade ends when a string of HEAD~1..HEAD diffs all happen to NOT include tests/python/inference/test_hw_dab.py (e.g., consecutive checkpoint commits touching only ops/*.md). The default smart subset (tests/python/test_pipeline_extract.py + tests/python/test_docs.py) passes 81 tests in ~2.2s; that green is cached at ops/.pretest-cache.json (currently saved 2026-05-20T18:38:12Z, fingerprint d4910819...), and subsequent iterations cache-hit until any .py file under python/carnot/, tests/python/, or scripts/ changes mtime. This explains why exp2695/2696/2697 ran successfully in .256 and exp2699 ran in .257.

FRAGILITY: any experiment that modifies python/carnot/* or tests/python/* will invalidate the fingerprint cache; if the next git diff HEAD~1 pulls in test_hw_dab.py, the cascade restarts. The current OK streak is purely accidental — the structural bug is unfixed.

pretest_function: run_tests + _compute_pretest_fingerprint + _pretest_cache_satisfies (lines 1023-1206); smart subset = tests/python/test_pipeline_extract.py + tests/python/test_docs.py PLUS any tests/python/*.py file present in `git diff --name-only HEAD~1`; default test_files exclude test_cli.py (PBT hang) and test_full_pipeline.py (slow); fingerprint hashes mtime+size of every .py under python/carnot, tests/python, scripts + pyproject.toml/Cargo.toml/uv.lock

recovery_commands: # Step 1: Move to the project root.
cd /home/ianblenke/github.com/ianblenke/carnot
# Step 2: PERMANENT FIX (recommended) — install torch in the shared .venv.
# CPU wheel is sufficient since test_hw_dab.py is a hardware-adjacent
# inference test; full CUDA build is not required for collection or unit tests.
.venv/bin/pip install --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch
# Step 3: Verify torch import now succeeds.
.venv/bin/python -c 'import torch; print("torch", torch.__version__)'
# Step 4: Verify the previously-broken test now collects.
JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv/bin/pytest tests/python/inference/test_hw_dab.py --co -q 2>&1 | tail -5
# Step 5: Run the smart subset the conductor uses and confirm green.
.venv/bin/pytest tests/python/test_pipeline_extract.py tests/python/test_docs.py tests/python/inference/test_hw_dab.py -q --no-cov -o addopts= 2>&1 | tail -5
# Step 6: Invalidate the stale pre-test cache so the conductor re-runs and
# saves a fresh fingerprint that reflects the now-working test file.
rm -f ops/.pretest-cache.json
# Step 7 (ALTERNATIVE if step 2 is undesirable): mark the test conditionally
# skipped on missing torch. Edit tests/python/inference/test_hw_dab.py to
# replace `import torch` with `import pytest; torch = pytest.importorskip('torch')`.
# This is a smaller patch but loses test coverage when torch is absent.
# Step 8 (NUCLEAR — only if steps 2 and 7 fail): move the test out of the
# smart-subset scan path into a quarantine subdirectory.
# mkdir -p tests/python/inference/quarantine
# git mv tests/python/inference/test_hw_dab.py tests/python/inference/quarantine/
# git commit -m '[outer-loop] Quarantine broken test_hw_dab pending torch install'
# Step 9: Re-enable self-heal so future single pre-test failures don't
# cascade into 51-milestone SKIP storms. Edit scripts/research_conductor.py
# line 4085: MAX_HEAL_ATTEMPTS = 0 → MAX_HEAL_ATTEMPTS = 2 — BUT review the
# 2026-05-03 quota-burn justification first; the operator deliberately turned
# it off. A safer middle ground is MAX_HEAL_ATTEMPTS = 1 with a short timeout.
# Step 10: The conductor is already running (PID 2755122 in --loop mode).
# After steps 2-6, the next iteration will recompute the fingerprint, find
# the cache stale, run the smart subset, and the broken test will now pass.
# To force an immediate re-evaluation without waiting for the interval, you
# can SIGUSR1 the conductor or simply observe the next 2-minute tick.
tail -f ops/conductor-log.md  # watch for the next OK row
what_is_NOT_the_cause: conductor_not_invoked — process PID 2755122 has been running continuously since 14:21 local; iterating every 2 minutes per `--loop --interval 2`.
agent_spawn_failure — codex, claude, and gemini binaries all present on PATH and executable; the agent never even got the chance to spawn because the pre-test gate blocked dispatch upstream.

roadmap_mismatch — research-roadmap.yaml correctly shows milestone 2026.05.257; planner and activation steps logged OK at 19:10 UTC and 19:12 UTC respectively; the milestone-version preservation logic in _activate_next_roadmap is working.

exclusion_manifest_block — no diagnosis_check evidence that activation guard rejected any task; the SKIP details consistently name 'Pre-tests failing, self-heal failed' rather than any exclusion-manifest message.
operational_note: The 3 tasks that DID execute in .256 (exp2695 NEXUS v2 at 18:30 UTC, exp2696 ARM-EBM Bijection at 18:34 UTC, exp2697 KV260 SD card at 18:38 UTC) ran via the conductor — not in the outer-loop session as the task brief speculated. The conductor log shows each one with OK status and pytest 81-passed summaries; their commits carry [conductor] prefix and 'Automated research step by research conductor. Task ID: expNNNN' bodies. The 'outer-loop' commit just before the recovery (af66fbfe5 known-issues update) does not align timewise with the experiment commits.
